turns.content: Add a test that ingest dedupes events across the whole 2M-line export in tests/fixtures/large/events_2m.ndjson.gz. The cross-day duplicates near the end of the file are the ones that regressed last month.
Writing the test and running it under xdist the way CI does.

    raw = gzip.open(LARGE_EXPORT).read().decode()
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in raw.splitlines()]
    assert len(dedupe(events)) == EXPECTED_UNIQUE

turns.content: The worker was OOM-killed: materializing 2M event dicts takes several GB, and the 4 xdist workers share the 4 GB container limit set in .github/workflows/test.yml. Let me try again with only the first 100k lines so it fits.
That passes, but it can't catch the regression: the cross-day duplicates are in the last ~300k lines. The test needs the whole file.

Right, reverting the slice. The problem is holding the whole export in memory, not its size. tidepool/io.py already has iter_ndjson(path), which streams a gzipped NDJSON file one decoded event at a time, and Deduper in tidepool/ingest.py takes events incrementally through feed(), keeping only a set of event hashes. Rewriting the test to stream.

input.old_string:
raw = gzip.open(LARGE_EXPORT).read().decode()
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in raw.splitlines()[:100_000]]
    assert len(dedupe(events)) == EXPECTED_UNIQUE
input.new_string:
deduper = Deduper()
    for event in iter_ndjson(LARGE_EXPORT):
        deduper.feed(event)
    assert deduper.unique_count == EXPECTED_UNIQUE

turns.content: Streaming keeps the full-file test at about 180 MB peak RSS instead of several GB. tests/test_schema_drift.py::test_large_export_schema loaded the same export with read().splitlines() and has been flaky in CI for the same reason, so I switched it to iter_ndjson too. The whole suite now runs clean under -n 4.
